summary: Native agent mailboxes preserve canonical send order across graph and message-shard mail and replay pending offers when the same incarnation reconnects.

replay.detail: A transport reconnect reoffers pending messages whose staging was admitted by a native binding for this incarnation. Receipt timestamps alone do not establish native custody. Historical and unfenced offers remain excluded, including legacy staging without provenance.

schema.detail: Additive daemon-local native staging provenance for graph claims and marks; shard lifecycle records carry the checked incarnation in local fields. Legacy records default to no native custody proof. No client-v0 schema, codegen, published schema or contract digest change.

rules.detail: No authority, retention or claim-admission change.

compatibility.detail: Full native mailbox snapshots and incremental updates use canonical send keys across both stores. Pagination namespaces are not delivery priority. Socket epochs and durable boot floors are logged on open and close; delivery-assessment transitions log their cause.

downtime.detail: Ordinary rolling deployment; no data conversion.

recovery.detail: Pending native offers remain owned by their harness incarnation across transport reconnects. Unresolved staged recovery batches are reconstructed before choosing more backlog, preserving the five-outstanding bound. Message IDs and existing receipt idempotency preserve deduplication. Legacy or unfenced staging is not retroactively attributed to a native incarnation; polling retains its existing local offer policy.
